$comment: Quality gates run by the Stop hook (cratis-quality-gate.sh).
Data, not code: a consuming repository overrides this file (or points CRATIS_HOOKS_GATES at
its own) without touching the script. Gates run in order and stop at the first failure.
A gate runs only when the working tree contains a change matching one of its "changed" globs,
AND every entry in "requires" is satisfied, AND its project was discovered. Any of those
unsatisfied makes the gate a NO-OP with a message on stderr — that is how a repo that has no
.NET, no frontend, or no source at all stays quiet.
Gate fields:
id               stable identifier, shown in failure output
description      one line, shown in the dry-run plan
changed          globs (repo-relative) that must match a changed file for the gate to run
excludeChanged   globs that never count as a relevant change
requires.commands executables that must be on PATH
requires.paths   repo-relative literal paths that must all exist (no globbing)
requires.packageScripts  package.json scripts that must be defined in the gate's working directory
(a g: script may instead be defined in the repository root package.json, which assumes
Yarn Berry, where a root-defined g: script runs from every workspace; no workspace
package.json is inspected); a missing script makes the gate a NO-OP instead of a
"Couldn't find a script" failure
workingDirectory repo-relative directory the command runs in
workingDirectoryFrom  globs identifying the project file this gate builds; the command runs
in that file's directory, and a repository holding none makes the gate a
NO-OP. Globs are tried in order, so the list states a preference. Ignored
when workingDirectory is set. Discovery excludes the installed .cratis/ai tree
when .cratis/ai.manifest.json exists, including symlinks resolving into that tree.
Symlinks outside the task-owning repository are never discovered. Without the install
manifest the corpus is authored source and its packages remain eligible. Within each
glob the deepest project containing a changed file wins, else the first sorted match.
command          argv array — executed directly, never through a shell (no eval)
Managed corpus and adapter trees (.cratis/**, .pi/**, .claude/**) never count as a relevant change:
a corpus update must not run a repository's application gates over files that are not its application.
No gate names a product's solution, package or source root — a default that does would
silently no-op in every repository except the one it was written for. The .NET and frontend
gates discover the repository's own solution/package instead, so they activate unchanged in
an application repository, a framework repository, and (as nothing to run) in a corpus-only
repository. An empty plan reports that no product verification was performed.
The override model, in order of increasing force: a repository states only what differs in its
own .cratis/ai/quality-gates.project.json, which the runner merges over this file by gate id
(a project fact belongs there, never edited into this managed file, or the next managed update
reports drift or discards it); or it points CRATIS_HOOKS_GATES at a file anywhere. Neither
requires a script fork. The merge is shallow: a field the override states replaces the managed one.
The one exception: an override that sets "command" without "requires" also drops this gate's
requires.packageScripts, since those guard the managed command, not the override's.
Example .cratis/ai/quality-gates.project.json, for a repository whose frontend is not at the root:
{ "gates": [ { "id": "frontend-lint", "workingDirectory": "Source/App" } ] }
Commands are pinned to .cratis/ai/rules/general.md 'Quality Gates' and .cratis/ai/hooks/agent-stop.md.
Note the Release build passes -p:CratisProxiesOutputPath= per general.md so the proxy
generator does not re-run and touch already-correct generated files. That property is the
only gate: the generator's target is Condition="'$(CratisProxiesOutputPath)' != ''", and
there is no DisableProxyGenerator property — MSBuild accepts unknown -p: names silently,
so passing one looks effective and does nothing. The Debug gate deliberately omits the
override because general.md makes Debug the canonical proxy-regeneration trigger. A
consuming repository's own CI should split Debug and Release the same way.

gates.description: dotnet build (Debug) — compiles #if DEBUG spec code and regenerates the TypeScript proxies
dotnet build (Release) — build-only check, proxy generation skipped (general.md)
yarn g:compile:specs — zero TypeScript errors in specs
